pr_title: Fix polling interval bug in Overkiz integration
pr_body:
## Proposed change
Fixes #68620. A bug that we had for a long time, impacting all users outside of Europe. The coordinator would always reset the update_interval to 30 seconds, even though it should be 1 hour for some installations. This PR will fix this bug and add helper functions to make this more clear together with documented code.

After this PR, we will store the original update interval and we reset the interval to this original stored value.

Fixes https://github.com/iMicknl/ha-tahoma/issues/803 and https://github.com/iMicknl/ha-tahoma/issues/586, reported at the custom component.

review_comments:
Is this intentionally overwriting `original_update_interval` again? I was thinking about thie case where this function is called twice, then `_restore_update_interval` doesn't restore the original value anymore, it restores an updated original value.

Perhaps you could walk me through what is supposed to be happening in a little more detail if i'm mis-undertanding the cases since it seems like there may be multiple interesting cases being exercised here, but hard to confirm without tests exercising the issues.

Do you have an example of data update coordinator tests? I looked into that a while ago, but I was not able to get started 🙁.

The other comments I will have a look at tomorrow.

The tests for using an update coordinator can look like any integration. For example, when [updating an integration](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/74690/files) to use a coordinator I didn't need to change the tests really. But you can use google calendar as an example...

I added an extra check in 442019d3812c1f3c62ebe72bfaa0e84868b1e635 to only update the original interval if the new one is different. In theory this should not happen, but looking at the code and all events, it could happen when Somfy does not broadcast the events in order.

I'm still having a little trouble following since it seems like `original_update_interval` should just never be updated once its set, given the name "original". 

Given original is set in the constructor, can this function only update `self.update_interval = update_interval`?

I will look into this. @allenporter also noticed this, so I will have a better look and rework this PR.

For now I will mark it as a draft.
We don't allow 1 second update interval. Min 5 seconds for polling integrations.

This is current behavior in the integration (thus no new behavior), and this only happens for a maximum of 10 seconds. This is done to get instant state updates after executing a command on a stateful device. During this period it will poll every second to have instant state updates (and than restore to original interval). Somfy agreed with this by the way, so we are not overloading their service. (they actually do the same in their application...).

Would this be allowed in Home Assistant? There is no possibility to use a websocket or other subscriber/push method unfortunately.
No, we don't allow that. The service handler should just request a refresh. We shouldn't change the interval.
